affects.why: A Republican sweep would push yields and the dollar up and gold down; a slow count could lift gold as a haven (FXStreet, Admirals).
In a disputed result, high-beta tech would take the brunt; a Democratic House brings data-centre regulation risk (TradingKey).
US shares are ~62% of the fund; Hartnett's downside case is a US stock drop of 10% or more.

calendar.beat_record: The S&P 500 was higher 12 months after all 19 midterms since 1950 (Admirals).
downside: A Republican sweep is the 'unpriced' risk: higher long yields and dollar, lower gold (FXStreet).
A slow or disputed count would hit high-beta tech hardest (TradingKey).
calendar.expected: Prediction markets favour Democrats to win the House (~91%) and the Senate (~66%). Reuters (3 Nov): polls favour Democrats for the House; the Senate is seen as close.
calendar.priced: Republican sweep priced at only 7.5–9.4%. Admirals says a Democratic result is largely priced, so the first move could be muted.

result.headline: Democrats win the House and are projected to take the Senate; Nasdaq-100 futures fell as much as 2.2% then narrowed to about -0.6%
points: Democrats won the House (projected 235-252 seats) and at least 51 Senate seats after flipping six, including Texas and Ohio (Pomegra).
That was the 'blue sweep', which prediction markets had seen as likely for the House but closer for the Senate.
Tech fell hardest overnight on fears of tighter data-centre rules: Nvidia about -1.5%, Amazon lower (Yahoo/Stocktwits).
Dollar and US yields fell, gold rose 0.5% (Reuters) - mixed for your pie: SGLN up, but a firmer pound trims the sterling value of US holdings.
Analysts expect hearings and investigations more than laws that stop data-centre building (Reuters, Stifel).

upside: A split Congress: 'gridlock is Goldilocks' for shares (BofA's Hartnett).

affects.why: A rate decision that moves the pound changes the sterling value of your dollar holdings and pie funds (Pound Sterling Live).

calendar.beat_record: Because November is fully priced, weaker UK data would hit December odds first (FXStreet).
downside: A hold 'would be a sharp surprise', sending GBP/USD towards 1.32 (Tradingnews).
A tighter budget could ease pressure to hike, softening the pound (Admirals).
calendar.event: Bank of England rate decision + Monetary Policy Report
calendar.expected: A rise from 3.75% to 4.00%: 54 of 63 economists in a Reuters poll expect it, after September inflation came in at 3.5% vs 3.4% forecast. Goldman expects a 7-2 vote and inflation peaking above 4% early 2027 (investingLive).
calendar.priced: About 95–96% priced in SONIA futures, with ~48% odds of a second rise by December.

result.headline: Raised to 4.00% as expected, 8-1 vote (Mann wanted 4.25%); pound little changed at ~$1.347
points: Bank Rate up 0.25 points to 4.00%, the first rise since August 2023, matching the Reuters poll.
The vote was 8-1, with the only dissenter (Catherine Mann) wanting a bigger half-point rise; Goldman had forecast 7-2.
Inflation seen peaking around 4.9-5% by mid-2027; Bailey said another rise looks likely unless the Middle East conflict is resolved.
GBP/USD ended about $1.3473, barely changed, so little effect on the pound value of your US holdings; FTSE 100 -0.4%.

upside: A hike with hawkish guidance could take GBP/USD through 1.3408 towards 1.35 (Tradingnews).

affects.why: Strong data raises the odds of the 9 Dec Fed hike markets already expect (Forbes); higher rate odds have weighed on gold this month (Trading Economics).

calendar.beat_record: A miss of 100k+ typically moves the S&P 500 0.5–1.5% and the dollar about 0.5% in the first hour; unemployment, wages and revisions can reverse it (FinanceCalendar).
downside: A strong number would firm up the December hike that is already 84% priced (FedWatch via Yardeni).
calendar.expected: About +59,000 jobs (forecasts 50,000 Barclays to 95,000 RSM); unemployment steady at 4.2%; Deutsche Bank sees wages +0.3% (Kiplinger). September added only 29k. Reuters poll (6 Nov): about +65,000 (range 35k–125k), unemployment 4.2%, wages +0.3% m/m and 2.9% y/y, the first sub-3% annual reading since May 2021.
calendar.priced: Prediction markets (14 Oct) put the median at about +55k jobs, range -10k to +125k.

result.headline: Much stronger than expected: +165,000 jobs, unemployment 4.1%
points: Payrolls +165,000 vs about 65,000 expected; September revised up to 60,000 (Kitco).
Unemployment fell to 4.1% from 4.2%; hourly pay +0.4% m/m vs 0.3% forecast, 3.1% y/y.
Strengthens the case for a December Fed hike; 2-year yields rose about 6bp to 4.53%.
Gold fell about 1%; Nasdaq still closed up 1.09% as chip stocks bounced (TheStreet).

upside: A weak number would lower the odds of the December Fed hike; falling December odds support gold and shares (Admirals).

calendar.beat_record: Zacks ESP +8.2%; average EPS surprise 23% over the last two quarters. EBITDA beat in 4 of 5 quarters, revenue missed in 4 of 5 (TIKR).
downside: The Texas governor-elect wants a data-centre moratorium; KeyBanc downgraded Vistra to Sector Weight on 4 Nov, saying it has the greatest exposure (Investing.com).
2027 revenue consensus cut ~4% since June; weaker Texas power forward prices; BMO cut its target to $210 (TIKR).
Texas holds about a quarter of US data-centre capacity due by 2030, and the new governor-elect ousted Abbott (Reuters).
calendar.expected: EPS ~$2.71–2.89, adjusted EBITDA ~$2.1bn (TIKR); 2026 EBITDA guidance $6.8–7.6bn reaffirmed. Revenue estimates vary widely ($6.7–7.8bn). Results before the US open, call 3pm UK. MarketBeat consensus: EPS $3.01, revenue $6.03bn; average analyst target $202.43. Zacks consensus: EPS $2.34, revenue $7.44bn; Zacks ESP +7.5% points to a likely beat.
means: Judge Vistra on adjusted EBITDA, not EPS: its EPS jumps around with hedging accounting. About $2.1bn is expected (TIKR).
It beat EBITDA forecasts in 5 of the 6 quarters with a forecast, yet the shares fell after 5 of the last 8 reports.
The call matters more than the quarter: management will update 2026 and 2027 guidance, and the CFO says 2027 is trending to the low end of $7.4-7.8bn.
Upside: the Meta nuclear deals and the Cogentrix purchase could add about $700m to 2027, and a government nuclear loan of up to $4.2bn is pending.
Options price about 8.3% either way (as of 3 Nov), well above its 5.3% 10-year average move (earnings-watcher).
You hold it for a few months, so this report sits inside your window.
past_notes: Q4 24: fell 12.3% on a day when AI and power stocks sold off broadly.
Q2 25: missed on EBITDA, fell 7% before the open, then closed up 2.4%.
calendar.priced: Options imply ±8–11%, about double its 10-year average (±5.3%); the actual move beat the implied move in only 4 of 18 reports.

result.headline: Beat on EBITDA and EPS, revenue missed; shares closed +10.55% at $124.80 (confirmed)
points: Adjusted EBITDA (ongoing ops) $2.38bn vs ~$2.1bn expected, up over 50% on a year ago (Vistra, TIKR).
Adjusted EPS $3.01 vs $2.71 consensus; revenue $6.35bn missed the $6.79bn expected (XTB).
2026 EBITDA guidance narrowed to $7.1–7.5bn with a higher midpoint; first 2027 range $7.7–8.5bn, above the $7.4–7.8bn the CFO had flagged; $1.5bn more buybacks.
Shares closed up 10.55% at $124.80 (StockAnalysis) from Thursday's 52-week low; XTB says investors focused on future cash flow, with about 98% of 2027 output hedged.
For your few-months holding: the report removed the near-term guidance-cut worry, though the stock is still well below its $203.66 high.

upside: The DOE nuclear loan (up to $4.2bn) and a 2026/27 guidance update on the call (TIKR).
calendar.watch_line: Shares fell 13.8% and then 6.2% into the report (to $112.87); options imply ±12.7% (earnings-watcher, 5 Nov).

affects.why: Hot inflation lifted rate-hike odds, which pushed gold to its lowest since July this week (Trading Economics).

calendar.beat_record: Treasury yields usually rise on a hot print and fall on a soft one (TickerVelocity).
downside: A hot print lifts yields; growth shares can suffer while financials outperform (TickerVelocity).
calendar.expected: Monthly: +0.3% headline and +0.2% core expected (FXEmpire, 8 Nov); RBC expects +0.3% / +0.3%; Cleveland Fed nowcast +0.24% / +0.21%. No yearly rate will be published for overall or core prices because October 2025 data were never collected. September: +0.6% m/m, 3.7% y/y.
calendar.priced: Markets price an 84% chance of a December Fed hike (CME FedWatch via Investing.com, 10 Nov), so a hot print mainly confirms it; a soft print would be the surprise.
upside: A soft print would pull yields down, which helps long-duration growth shares (TickerVelocity).

calendar.expected: No consensus in source. September: +1.3% m/m, +6.3% y/y; core +0.5% m/m.

affects.why: Nvidia is the All-World fund's largest holding at 5.0% (Vanguard).

calendar.beat_record: Beat EPS in 7 of the last 8 quarters (MarketBeat).
downside: Three customers are 44% of revenue; purchase commitments up to $279bn; gross margin guided lower; no China data-centre sales assumed (XTB).
The board opened an independent probe on 8 Nov into reports Huang was targeted by Chinese intelligence; House chairs want a briefing on 18 Nov (NBC, FourWeekMBA).
Trump said on 9 Nov the FBI is looking into Huang's relationship with the alleged spy, though he said he believes Huang (Al Jazeera).
calendar.expected: EPS $2.49, revenue $108.8bn (MarketBeat), just above Nvidia's own $108bn ±2% guide; gross margin guided 74%.

history_sources.name: Regards of Wall Street NVDA earnings moves

key_metrics.why: Beating its own guide is expected
Historically the main driver of the move

means: Nvidia guided $108bn revenue and a 74% gross margin; the consensus ($108.8bn) is only just above its own guide.
It beat in 7 of the last 8 quarters but the shares fell after 5 of them. What moves it is the outlook for the next quarter, not the beat.
Last quarter it rose 8.7% after guiding well above forecasts. That is the pattern to look for.
Its results also move your grid ETF and your Vanguard fund, where Nvidia is one of the largest holdings.
past_notes: Q1 FY26: EPS shown as a miss only because of a $4.5bn China export charge; underlying EPS $0.96 beat.
Q2 FY27 (Aug): rose 8.7% after guiding well above forecasts.
calendar.priced: Options not yet listed for the event. Its 10-year average results move is ±8.4% (2-year ±5.7%); last quarter options implied ±5.9% and it closed +8.7%.
upside: Last quarter's guide was well above consensus, and the CFO pointed to ~70% growth in FY28 vs ~44% expected (XTB).
calendar.watch_line: Watch: next quarter's revenue guide and gross margin

calendar.beat_record: Beat EPS in each of the last 4 quarters.
downside: Current bookings growth (cRPO) slowed to 12% from 18–20% and is expected to stay lower for several quarters; full-year guide midpoint was below consensus.
calendar.expected: Autodesk's own guide: revenue $2.125–2.140bn, non-GAAP EPS $3.04–3.09. Consensus ~$3.14 (Earnings Whispers).

key_metrics.why: It has beaten its guide every quarter here
Future contracted revenue: the market's worry
Cuts here would hit the shares

means: Autodesk beat forecasts in all 8 of the last quarters, but the shares rose after only 4.
In its last two reports it beat yet fell about 4% each time, because full-year guidance came in light and future contracted revenue (cRPO) slowed to 12% growth from 18-20%.
So the key numbers are cRPO and the free-cash-flow guide ($2.725-2.750bn for the year), not the EPS beat.
You hold it for a few months, so this report falls inside your holding window.
past_notes: Q1 and Q2 FY27: beat both times, but fell ~4% each time on light guidance and slowing cRPO.
calendar.priced: Options not yet listed. Last quarter implied ±9.4%; its 10-year average move is ±8.5% (2-year ±7.8%).
calendar.time: after US close (estimate; not yet confirmed)
upside: Subscription revenue grew 17% last quarter vs 14.5% expected; BofA calls second-half guidance conservative (Finviz).
calendar.watch_line: Watch: cRPO growth and full-year guidance

affects.why: Gold fell about 1% on Friday as hike odds rose

calendar.downside: A hike plus signals of more in early 2027 (Boston College's Bethune expects a further move)
calendar.expected: Futures price an 84% chance of a quarter-point hike (CME FedWatch via Investing.com, 10 Nov), up from about two-thirds before the jobs report
calendar.priced: Mostly priced in as a hike after October's 165,000 jobs
calendar.upside: A hold would go against what futures price (Beinsure)

markets.name: Nasdaq Composite
markets.note: US index of ~3,000 Nasdaq-listed shares, tech-heavy
markets.source: Yahoo Finance close (+2.74%); distance from high and YTD rolled forward from ChartRow's 6 Nov figures (-10.9%, +6.0%)

stories.headline: Trump says the FBI is looking into Jensen Huang's relationship with an alleged Chinese spy

impacts.why: Shares closed down 4.27% on Monday as the story broke; an outside-counsel inquiry ordered by the board is still reviewing the matter (source 1). Results are due 17 Nov.

sources.title: Trump says FBI probing Nvidia CEO Huang's affair with alleged spy

stories.summary: Speaking at the White House on Monday, President Trump said the FBI is looking into the Nvidia CEO's relationship with Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore data-centre firm Megaspeed whom US officials allege worked for Chinese intelligence. Trump said Huang told him he had no idea she was a spy, that he believed him, and that Huang would "be in good shape". Nvidia's board has said it has no reason to think company secrets or national security were compromised, and China's Foreign Ministry called the allegations a smear.

stories.headline: Grab's Malaysia AI-infrastructure venture with SoftBank and Petros put at $1.85bn to start

impacts.why: Grab is one of three partners, bringing its Southeast Asian app ecosystem and AI skills (source 2); no source gives Grab's share of the $1.85bn (source 1).

sources.title: Grab Holdings (GRAB) Joins $1.85B AI Infrastructure Initiative in Malaysia
SoftBank, Grab, Petros to explore AI infrastructure ecosystem development in Sarawak

stories.summary: GuruFocus reported on Monday that Grab, SoftBank Group and Sarawak's state oil company Petros are developing AI infrastructure across Sarawak and Peninsular Malaysia, with an initial $1.85bn investment and a goal of 5 gigawatts or more of computing capacity over several years. Spending is to be phased and tied to milestones and customer contracts. It builds on a framework agreement the three signed in October, which named no figures; Grab's own share of the cost is not given.

explainer.meaning: A US stock index of the 30 biggest chip designers, makers and equipment suppliers, used as the main gauge of chip shares.

stories.headline: Chip rally carries into Asia: Samsung and SK Hynix up over 5%, Nikkei above 60,000

impacts.why: Fell 4.2% on Monday to its lowest close since 7 April while the chip index rose nearly 7% (source 1).

sources.title: U.S. stock futures steady after tech-led rebound; CPI in focus

stories.summary: Monday's US chip surge, with the Philadelphia semiconductor index up nearly 7%, AMD up over 13% and Broadcom up 8.8%, spread to Asia on Tuesday. Korea's Kospi jumped about 5.2% at the open with Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix each up more than 5%, briefly triggering a curb on programme buying, and the Nikkei rose about 2.4% to 60,172. Nvidia was the exception on Monday, closing at its lowest level since 7 April.

explainer.meaning: How much computing capacity companies want to rent or build for AI, which drives orders for chips like Nvidia's and for cloud services like AWS and Google Cloud.

stories.headline: SoftBank's Japanese telecoms arm braces for a possible slowdown in US AI data-centre demand

sources.title: SoftBank Corp. CEO Said to Brace for Possible US AI Slowdown

stories.summary: Bloomberg reported that SoftBank Corp., the mobile arm of SoftBank Group, is preparing for a possible slowdown in US AI data-centre demand and may look elsewhere for growth. The company still raised its full-year forecasts, to ¥7.9 trillion revenue and ¥610bn net profit, with cloud and AI revenue up 37% year on year. Its SB Neo AI-cloud venture is due to launch in the year to March 2028.

explainer.meaning: Contracts that trade before the market opens and show where investors expect an index like the S&P 500 to start the day.

stories.headline: US futures steady after the S&P 500's best day since April; Nasdaq 100 futures flat

sources.title: U.S. stock futures steady after tech-led rebound; CPI in focus

stories.summary: By early Tuesday, S&P 500 futures were up 0.2% and Dow futures up 0.4%, while Nasdaq 100 futures were flat after Monday's rally (S&P 500 +2.4%, its best day since 8 April; Nasdaq +2.7%). Lower oil, after President Trump signalled further strikes on Iran were unlikely, helped Monday's move. Investors now turn to October CPI today, with CoreWeave, Cisco and Applied Materials results due this week as a read on data-centre spending.

explainer.meaning: The Louisiana pipeline hub whose price is the benchmark for US natural gas.

stories.headline: US natural gas jumps as much as 8.3% on colder forecasts and a short squeeze
stories.summary: Henry Hub natural gas futures rose as much as 8.3% on Monday, their biggest move in six weeks, on cooler weather forecasts and a short squeeze, while crude oil fell sharply. Gas is the fuel that usually sets wholesale power prices in Texas and other US markets.

explainer.meaning: A monthly measure of how much a typical basket of goods and services costs; a fast rise means inflation and can push central banks to raise rates.

stories.headline: US October CPI due at 1:30pm UK, with an 84% chance of a December Fed hike priced

sources.title: U.S. stock futures steady after tech-led rebound; CPI in focus
Gold rises almost 2% amid sliding dollar, slumping oil prices a day ahead of CPI

stories.summary: October consumer prices are out today at 8:30am New York time (1:30pm UK), followed by producer prices on Friday. CME FedWatch shows markets pricing an 84% chance of a quarter-point Fed hike in December after the strong jobs report. The usual yearly inflation rates will not be published because October 2025 prices were never collected during the government shutdown.

explainer.meaning: When short-term interest rates rise relative to long-term ones, often because markets expect the central bank to raise rates soon.

stories.headline: Treasury curve flattens: 2-year yield up to about 4.56%, 10-year at 4.88%
stories.summary: Short-dated US government bond yields rose about 3 basis points to roughly 4.56% on Monday while the 10-year settled at 4.88% and the 30-year at 5.28%, as markets lean towards a December Fed hike. A $58bn three-year note sale went at 4.627%, and a $42bn 10-year auction is due today.

topline: No new closes overnight: Nasdaq sits about 8.5% below its 6 Oct record and VWRP 5.0% below its 6 Oct high after Monday's rally.
Trump said the FBI is looking into Jensen Huang's relationship with an alleged Chinese spy but that he believes Huang; Nvidia closed Monday at its lowest since 7 April, with results due 17 Nov.
The chip rally spread to Asia (Samsung and SK Hynix +5%, Nikkei above 60,000); US futures are steady, Nasdaq 100 flat.
US October CPI lands at 1:30pm UK today, with an 84% chance of a December Fed hike already priced; no yearly rate will be published.
Grab's Malaysia AI venture with SoftBank and Petros was reported at $1.85bn to start, aiming for 5GW+ of computing.
